cues.en: Go next. Why? Why would I do that? Go next. And the reason is I was unfortunate enough to start struggling with some repetitive strain injury a couple years ago. And if you're not familiar, RSI is pain felt in your muscles, nerves, and tendons caused by repetitive and overuse. In our industry, that often means repetitive overuse of a keyboard or a mouse.
cues.zh: 下一张。为什么？我为什么要这么做？下一张。原因是我几年前不幸开始饱受重复性劳损的折磨。如果你不太了解，RSI 就是因重复动作和过度使用引起的肌肉、神经和肌腱疼痛。在我们的行业里，这通常意味着过度重复使用键盘或鼠标。

cues.en: And just out of curiosity, if you're willing to share and want to see in this room how many people have either experienced RSI or know someone who has experienced RSI, raise your hand. Yeah, so this is like a good majority of the room. Go next. So first, when I was injured, I tried taking breaks from typing. I tried yoga stretching. I wore the wrist braces. I tried massage, acupuncture, chiropractor. Go next.
cues.zh: 顺便好奇问一句，如果大家愿意分享的话，我想看看在座有多少人自己得过 RSI，或者认识得过 RSI 的人，请举手。看吧，现场绝大多数人都举手了。下一张。所以一开始受伤的时候，我试过暂停打字休息。我试了瑜伽拉伸。我戴了护腕。我还试过按摩、针灸、正骨。下一张。

cues.en: I tried pain creams, anti-inflammatories, muscle relaxers. I went through rounds of occupational and physical therapies. I even got trigger point injections which were as much fun as they sound. Go next. I had an ergonomic evaluation which is where you have this fancy ergo evaluator come to your workstation and tell you that everything needs to be 90 degrees and you should maybe stand desk and you should have a split keyboard and like all this stuff. So did all that, got the split keyboard.
cues.zh: 我试过止痛膏、消炎药、肌肉松弛剂，做过好几轮职业治疗和物理治疗，甚至还打了激痛点封闭针，那酸爽正如你所想。下一页。我还做了人体工学评估，就是请高级工学评估师来你的工位，告诉你所有角度都得保持90度，可能还得用升降桌，换分体键盘等等这一堆东西。于是我都照做了，买了分体键盘。

cues.en: Two trackball mice so I can split the load, right hand, left hand, go next. cues.en: Really excited about that. But so more about Talon. It's programmatically configured with Python. So all of the commands that you see are not just baked into Talon itself. cues.en: So if you start with the letter keys, you think you might say A and get A, or B, get B, right? But there's a problem with that. A lot of the letters in the alphabet, as pronounced, sound very similar to each other, so A-H-J-K.

cues.en: BCDEGPTVZ all sound very close, and I'm sure everyone here has been on a phone call where you've had to say, M is in Mike, or N is in Nancy, or I is in ice cream, or something silly, because it's really hard to spell a word and have it clearly understood. So I don't want that kind of trouble with my voice dictation that I'm going to have to be correcting myself all the time. Go next. So the solution is to
cues.zh: B、C、D、E、G、P、T、V、Z 听起来都差不多，我相信在座各位打电话时都遇到过这种情况，你得说“M 代表 Mike”或者“N 代表 Nancy”，或者“I 代表 ice cream”之类的傻话，因为想把单词拼清楚且让对方听明白真的很困难。所以我可不想在语音听写时遇到这种麻烦，还得老去纠错。下一页。所以解决办法就是

cues.en: pick a set of words that are phonetically different enough from each other that they're not going to be confused. There is an alphabet like this that exists already, the NATO phonetic alphabet. And this is a common question we get. Why not use the phonetic alphabet? And the reason is not because of accuracy, but because of speed. A lot of these words, except for golf, are more than one syllable. So I don't want to say November over and over again, right? Like, nah. So we design our own alphabet. Go next.
cues.zh: 挑一组在发音上差异足够大、不会混淆的词。其实已经存在这样一套字母表了，就是北约音标字母。这也是我们经常被问到的问题：为什么不用北约音标字母呢？原因不在于准确率，而在于速度。除了 golf 之外，这些词大多都不止一个音节。我可不想反反复复念 November，对吧？肯定不想。所以我们设计了自己的字母表。下一页。

cues.en: This is the alphabet I use. It's mostly based on an alphabet that was put together by the author of Talon, who spent a lot of time finding words that wouldn't be confused with each other. cues.zh: 我们把刚才学到的东西拓展一下，看看我日常在文本编辑器里写代码、用 git、把代码推送到 GitHub 时是什么样子的，这样大家也能更深入地了解这一切是如何协同工作的。顺便说明一下，有人问过我是不是给视频加速了。没有。这就是正常速度。而且没有任何剪辑。就是我按下录制，然后点击结束。

cues.en: It is more rehearsed than probably the code i write on a day-to-day. But this demo isn't about showing you how fast i say things. It's more about showing you what the tool can do. So go next.

cues.en: Go next. The learning curve. It's a little bit steep. We are so used to touch-based models, keyboards, and mice. It's a completely different part of your body you're using. It can be a little bit of a learning curve to get started. Also, it's pretty new in the space. There's some conventions starting to form, but in general, most of us have a bespoke setup where we've kind of globbed some scripts together, written some ourselves.
cues.zh: 下一页。学习曲线。确实稍微有点陡。我们太习惯基于触觉的交互模式、键盘和鼠标了。用语音相当于动用了完全不同的身体部位。刚上手的时候确实需要适应一下。另外，这在这个领域还算挺新的。虽然开始形成一些规范了，但大体上，我们大多数人都是自己拼凑的方案，东拼西凑合一些脚本，或者自己写一部分。

cues.en: Hopefully, over time, these start to become a little bit more standardized, and there's more tools that are built to help you learn and all that. But it still is a little bit steep. Go next. But some tips. Make sure you set aside some dedicated learning time. So what I did is I set aside a couple weeks. I just want to focus on this, and that's it. I'm not going to write any code that's going to be shipped anywhere. I'm just going to dedicate my time to learning. I picked some code in my code base that was going to be pretty similar to what I'd be writing, and I just tried copying it.
cues.zh: 希望随着时间的推移，这些能变得更标准化一些，也会有更多工具来帮助大家学习等等。但目前门槛还是有点高。看下一页。不过有些建议。一定要留出专门的学习时间。我当时的做法是留出了两周时间。我就想专心搞这个，别的什么都不做。我不写任何要上线的代码。我只把时间花在学习上。我在代码库里挑了一些和我平时写的很像的代码，然后尝试照着敲一遍。

cues.en: And that was a really great way for me to try it and then iterate on my talent set up and then keep going until I felt like I had some sort of efficiency. One thing that's really difficult is if you're injured and you're trying to learn this stuff, it requires typing to learn it, but you're trying to learn it so you don't have to type, and it's kind of a chicken and egg problem. If you have some friends that don't mind pairing on this with you to be your hands for this part of it, I recommend that. I don't generally otherwise recommend that you should
cues.zh: 这对我来说是个极好的尝试方式，我可以借此迭代我的 Talon 配置，一直练到我觉得自己达到了一定效率为止。有一点非常棘手的是，如果你受了伤并想学这套东西，你得打字才能学会它，但你学它又是为了不用打字，这有点像先有鸡还是先有蛋的问题。如果有朋友不介意和你结对，在这部分充当你的双手，我很推荐这么做。除此之外我通常不建议

cues.en: Try to get people to type for you if you're injured. It's kind of, I don't know. I have opinions about that. But for this in particular, yes. Find friends to help pair with. Remove time pressures. So what I mean by that is don't take on a big refactor while you're trying to also learn to voice code. You're going to underestimate how much time you spend thinking while you're working. And you're probably going to miss a lot of stuff, because instead of focus on your code, you're focused on inputting the code.
cues.zh: 在受伤时找人替你打字。这有点，我不知道该怎么说。我对此持保留态度。但对于这件事，确实可以。找朋友一起结对帮忙。排除时间压力。我的意思是，不要一边试图学习语音编程，一边接下繁重的重构任务。你会低估自己在工作时花在思考上的时间。而且你很可能会遗漏很多东西，因为你没有专注于代码本身，而是把精力都放在了如何把代码输入进去。

cues.en: So take easy tickets, take things that aren't time sensitive. Also, communication with your team. Work with your team to make sure that any communication that doesn't have to happen in real time in Slack, in a long scroll, move it to the GitHub PR. Move it to the Jira ticket instead so that you aren't in a position where you either have to reach for a keyboard or you're left behind in the conversation. My team has been very supportive of all of this, so thank you to my wonderful team out there.
cues.zh: 多接一些简单的任务，选那些不急的活儿。还有，注意和团队的沟通。和你的团队配合好，只要是不需要在 Slack 里长篇大论即时聊的沟通，都尽量移到 GitHub PR 里去。或者移到 Jira 工单里，这样你就不会陷入两难——要么非得去敲键盘，要么就跟不上讨论。我的团队对此非常支持，非常感谢我棒极了的团队。

cues.en: Also, leverage the talent community. There are other people like me. I'm not the only one. We all hang out in the talent slack, and we're happy to help and share our scripts and everything. So go next.
cues.zh: 另外，善用 Talent 社区。还有很多像我一样的人，我并不是特例。我们都活跃在 Talent 的 Slack 频道里，都很乐意提供帮助、分享我们的脚本和各种资源。好，下一张幻灯片。

cues.en: Tools with poor accessibility. So this is probably my biggest challenge right now. Most of the time when I have trouble using a thing with voice, it's not because of my tool set or my setup. It's most often the most frustrating things are when I'm working on a tool or a website that was not built with accessibility guidelines. And those are things that I can't fix myself.
cues.zh: 无障碍支持很差的工具。这大概是我目前面临的最大挑战。大多数时候，当我用语音操作遇到困难时，并不是因为我的工具集或配置有问题。最常发生、也最让人崩溃的情况，其实是我在用的工具或网站根本没按无障碍指南来开发。而这些问题我是无法自己修复的。

cues.en: And I have to spend a lot of time trying to work around. And it puts me in really awkward situations. I have some right now where our team relies on tools that I cannot use without a keyboard or mouse. And I have to either, I don't know, go plead to the company and be like, hey, can you really prioritize this? Or do I make the entire team, we have to shift to a whole other thing just because of me? It's not great. So go next. I have some requests for you all.
cues.zh: 我不得不花大量时间去想办法绕过它们。这让我陷入非常尴尬的境地。我现在就遇到过这种情况：我们团队依赖的一些工具，如果没有键盘或鼠标我就根本无法使用。那我该怎么办？跑去恳求开发公司说：“嘿，能不能优先解决这个问题？”还是说，就为了我一个人，要让整个团队大费周章地换用另一套完全不同的东西？这感觉糟透了。那进入下一页，我对大家有一些小小的恳求。

cues.en: that you should make accessibility a priority. Don't lock out users from using whatever you're building. Follow accessibility guidelines. There's a lot of great resources out there. There's some really great talks at this conference, even. So educate yourselves. It really shouldn't be the afterthought. Build your software as if you might need it someday. Because I certainly didn't expect to be here. I don't want to be ominous, but maybe I'm being ominous. I didn't expect to be here.
cues.zh: 一定要把无障碍性放在首位。不要把你正在构建的产品将用户拒之门外。请遵循无障碍指南。这方面有大量优质资源。甚至在本次大会上就有一些非常棒的演讲。所以去学习一下吧。它真的不应该成为事后才考虑的事。在构建软件时，把它当作你未来某天也可能会用到的东西来做。因为我当初也完全没料到自己会陷入这种境地。我不想危言耸听，但也许我听起来确实有点。我真的没料到自己会走到这一步。

cues.en: And you don't know what is ahead of you in the future. And build the tools that you would want if you were in a situation of needing those accessibility features. So go next. Voice strain. So what happens if you talk to your computer for eight hours a day? You might put some strain on your vocal cords. Go next. But there are ways to help with that. Stay hydrated. You notice I have my water up here.
cues.zh: 你永远不知道未来会发生什么。去构建那些如果你身处需要这些无障碍功能的环境中，你自己也会想用的工具。切到下一页。用嗓过度。如果你一天对着电脑讲八个小时的话，会发生什么？你的声带可能会承受过大的负担。下一页。但有一些方法可以缓解这种情况。保持水分。大家注意到了我这里放着水。

cues.en: If you are working in a dry climate, you might get a humidifier. That helps. I have one at home. Don't whisper and don't shout. So it turns out, shouting is kind of obvious, but whispering is more of a strain on your voice than talking at a normal tone. Some people will get voice coaches. So you hire someone much like singers or whatnot have voice coaches to teach them how to use their instrument and keep it healthy and get your wear on it.
cues.zh: 如果你在干燥的气候下工作，可以买个加湿器。挺管用的，我家里就有一个。不要耳语，也不要大喊大叫。事实证明，大喊大叫伤嗓子很明显，但其实耳语比用正常语调说话更费嗓子。有些人会请发声教练。就像歌手之类的会请教练教他们如何发声、保持嗓音健康并减少声带磨损一样。

cues.en: That's also an option. Go next. Go next. Open offices. So I'm not here to add to the pile of opinions about whether open offices are good or bad. But adding a microphone is a little bit of a challenge. There are solutions, though. So I'm going to walk you through a few. Go next. A steno mask. So I did not know these existed. And every picture I found of these was interesting.
cues.zh: 这也是一种选择。下一页。下一页。开放式办公室。我在这里不是要对开放式办公室的好坏发表意见。但是加个麦克风确实有点挑战。不过还是有解决方案的。接下来我就带大家看几种。下一页。速记面罩。我以前都不知道还有这种东西。而且我找到的每一张相关照片都挺有意思的。

cues.en: But they're very useful, and people like me and other voice coding folks find them really useful. They are good for dealing with background noise and giving you privacy in what you're saying. So for open offices, you might get some people going, what are you doing? But they do work, and they do work really well. These are actually the marketing pictures for these as well. So go next.
cues.zh: 但它们非常有用，我和其他用语音写代码的人都觉得很好用。它们很适合用来应对背景噪音，还能保证你说话的隐私。所以在开放式办公室里，可能会有人好奇你在干嘛？但它们确实管用，而且效果非常好。这些其实也是它们的宣传照。继续看下一张。

cues.en: So i know at least one person whose company bought him a fancy Glass cube that he gets to work in with sound proofing and everything that's very Cool. So this is another option if your company has some Money to buy you a cube. Go next. Remote work. So i do have an office, or i do have a Desk in our office and i go in sometimes. I've got a little space sort of off to the side.
cues.zh: 我知道至少有一个人的公司给他买了个高档的玻璃隔音舱，他在里面工作，隔音等各种配置一应俱全，非常酷。所以如果你们公司有预算给你买个隔音舱，这也是一种选择。继续下一张。远程办公。我在公司确实有一间办公室，或者说在办公室有个工位，我偶尔会去。我有个稍微偏一点的小角落。

cues.en: peers have called it the place where you might put a Xerox machine, but it works for me. Otherwise, I'm at home because when I'm at home, it turns out it's better for me actually to be away from my keyboard so I don't try and touch it. So I'm on the floor. I'm laying on pillows. I might be deploying software from Warrior II yoga pose, whatever. So yeah, I thank you fastly for being so great with remote workers. Go next. Not so big challenges.
cues.zh: 同事们开玩笑说这里原本可能是放施乐复印机的地方，但对我挺合适的。其他时候我都在家，因为在家的话，我发现自己离键盘远点反而更好，这样我就不会总想着去敲它。所以我常坐地上，靠着枕头，甚至可能摆着瑜伽的“战士二式”在那部署软件，怎么舒服怎么来。所以真的很感谢 Fastly 对远程办公人员这么友好。来看下一页，没那么难的挑战。

cues.en: These are things that I thought would be hard, but they actually aren't. So supporting specific programming languages. I thought I'd need to build up a whole library stuff just for Pearl or a whole library for Go or whatever. But it turns out, if I want to write Go tomorrow, I can just start writing Go. Of course, there will be things that I find that I might want to optimize, but they're just optimizations. There's nothing like I have to spend a bunch of time to build up support just to start using another language.
cues.zh: 这些是我原本以为会很难、但实际上并非如此的事。比如支持特定的编程语言。我本来以为得专门为 Perl 或 Go 等语言搭建整套库支持。但事实证明，如果我明天想写 Go，直接上手写就行。当然，后续可能会发现一些需要优化的细节，但那些只是优化而已。完全不需要在用新语言前花大量时间去搭一套支持体系。

cues.en: The other one is building tools with talent. So this has been surprisingly fun and easy. I've built a lot of my own tools myself. And they're like quick, easy wins. And I've built anything from just shortcuts for certain key commands to entire web views that will pop up to show me what commands do I have for Git or what commands do I have for this other thing. So it's really powerful. And you just save it to your talent directory. And it's loaded in talent and ready to go. It's pretty great. Go next.
cues.zh: 另一个则是用 Talent 构建工具。这一过程出奇地有趣且轻松。我自己打造了许多专属工具。它们带来的都是些立竿见影的小成效。我做过的东西五花八门，从某些按键命令的快捷方式，到弹出的完整 Web 视图——用来提示我 Git 有哪些命令，或者其他东西有哪些可用指令。所以它非常强大。你只需把它保存到 Talent 目录下，它就会加载进 Talent 随时待命。真的很棒。看下一页。

cues.en: So why? I want to revisit why I'm here, why I'm doing all of this, why am I talking to my computer, and why am I here telling you about it? And I want to remind everyone that this isn't just some weird software that's funny to hear and interesting. It's literally what gives me access to my career and to my computer. Think about what it would be like if tomorrow you lost access to your computer.
cues.zh: 那么，为什么要做这些？我想重新谈谈我为什么会站在这里，为什么要做这一切，为什么我要对着电脑说话，又为什么要在这里把这些讲给你们听？我想提醒大家的是，这不仅仅是一款听起来滑稽、有趣的奇特软件。它真真切切地赋予了我使用电脑、从事自身职业的能力。试想一下，如果明天你无法再使用电脑，生活会变成什么样？

cues.en: How much of your life is in that device, right? So this is what gives people like me or people who are otherwise unable to use a keyboard or mouse access. So it's very important. Go next.
